executive_assessment.text: The World Bank summary projects economic losses could reach 17% of GDP by 2050 without reforms, diversification and climate action; it also reports health costs rising from US$92 million in 2010 to US$260 million by 2050.
The NDC assesses hydropower as moderately exposed to climate hazards, particularly uneven rainfall and drought, because generation depends on surface-water availability and river flows.

The World Bank summary lists climate-ready health and education services, disease surveillance, climate-smart agriculture and forest management among proposed priorities; these are recommendations, not verified delivery.

geographic_notes.text: Congo River basin; Coastal zone: The NDC describes repeated low river-water levels and identifies coastal flooding, erosion, submersion and salinization among risks to coastal areas; it says sea-level rise was not yet perceptible in the assessment.

Congo River corridor; Oubangui River corridor; Brazzaville; Pointe-Noire: The IMF report says major floods have become more recurrent, affecting the river corridor and Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire; the Congo and Oubangui reached record levels during the 2023–2024 rainy season.

Nine departments, mainly northern regions bordering the Congo River: For December 2023 floods across nine departments, initial government estimates as of January 2024 counted 336,560 people affected and 23 deaths; homes, schools, health centers, water and sanitation were disrupted, and farming and fishing halted.

The 2023 flood impact counts are preliminary estimates, and no post-event independent validation was inspected.
